rooms.203070: Here the wall-walk swells into a small paved landing over the inner gate, where a squat stairhead roofed in grey slate shelters the top of the stair down to The Gate Of The Inner City. An iron brazier on a tripod stands by the stairhead door, its ashes stirring in the wind, and a rack of ash-shafted spears leans against the parapet. The battlements run on east and west from the landing, and beyond the inner edge the roofs of the city lie spread in a patchwork of tile and smoke.
rooms.2901: Narrow arrow slits pierce the parapet here, set at the height of a kneeling archer and splayed wide on the inner face, tight as a finger on the outer. The flagstones are worn into shallow troughs by generations of boots, and rainwater lies in them after every shower. The walk goes on east along the crenels and back west toward the stairhead above the gate.
rooms.2902: A banner of the city hangs from an iron pole socketed in the parapet, its colours bleached by the sun and its hem frayed to ribbons by the wind. The pole creaks in its bracket with every gust. Out past the crenels the plains roll away in squares of field and fallow, cut by the pale thread of the Trade Road. The wall bends round a corner a little way east, and west lies the way back to the gate.
rooms.2903: The wall turns here at a hard angle, the parapet swelling into a rounded buttress that juts out over the foot of the wall. A stone bench is built into the inner side, its seat polished by sitters, and the gusts drop away in the lee of the corner. The walk leads west along the battlements and south along the next long run of wall. Far across the plains the hills lie low and blue.
rooms.2904: A beacon stack stands on a round iron grate in the middle of the walk, a heap of tar-blackened logs under a tarred canvas hood, waiting for the night it must be lit. Soot streaks the stone around it up to the height of the crenels. Below the inner side the long roof of a timber warehouse shows, with a cart track running past it toward the market. The wall runs north toward the corner and south along the parapet.
rooms.2905: Someone has cut a row of initials and tally marks into the soft stone of a merlon at shoulder height, the oldest worn round and shallow, the newest still sharp and white. A rain barrel stands at the foot of the parapet, its lid weighted with a flat stone. The wind slides along the wall here carrying the smell of cut grass from the fields beyond. Battlements stretch away both north and south.
rooms.2906: The paving beneath your boots turns from pale grey to a darker, newer flagging where the walk was relaid, the join marked by a ridge of mortar like a scar. Iron spikes crown the outer parapet to discourage climbers, rust bleeding down the stone below each one. Over the rooftops of the inner side the Temple dome shows as a green copper hemisphere catching the light. North the walk runs back along the battlements, and south it reaches a stairhead tower.
rooms.203071: A stout tower stands over the gate here, its iron-banded oak door opening on the head of a stair that winds down to The Gate To The Inner City. A brazier burns in a blackened basket beside the door, and a water butt and a stack of kindling sit under a lean-to roof. Inward, the footbridge between the gate towers spans the heavy gate like a stitched seam. From the tower the walk leads north and south along the crenellated wall.
rooms.2907: A catapult emplacement fills a widened bay of the wall here, a squat stone platform ringed with low sandbags. The throwing engine rests cocked beneath a tarpaulin, its arm bound down with a rope as thick as a wrist, and pale scars from its wheels are cut deep into the flags. A pyramid of round stone shot waits beside it. The walk goes on north and south past the platform.
rooms.2908: A narrow shrine niche is cut into the inner parapet, hardly deeper than a hand, where a small figure of a woman holding a lamp is carved from the stone itself. Stubs of candles and a few withered flowers lie on the sill, stirred by the wind. Lichen has crept up from the sill around the figure like a green shawl. The wall-walk runs on to the north and to the south.
rooms.2909: A stretch of the outer parapet the length of a cart is built of newer, yellower stone, its courses neat against the weathered grey on either side. A mason's mark, a hammer and a square, is cut in the corner block of the mended breach. Beyond it the ground slopes away to a ditch, its bank trampled and scorched by some old assault. You can follow the wall north or south from here.
rooms.2910: A square watchtower rises from the wall here and the walk passes through its open archway, the vault above streaked with old rain and soot. A wooden bench runs along one wall of the passage, and an arrow loop looks out over the fields. The door of the tower's upper room is barred and shut fast. Beyond the arch the battlements continue north and south.
rooms.2911: A wooden pigeon loft on stilts stands against the inner parapet, its slatted face stuffed with straw and its perches white with droppings. The little doors are hooked open, and the cote is silent and empty. A wicker message basket hangs from a nail beside the door. The walk heads off north along the crenels, and south as well.
rooms.2912: From the inner parapet the whole market lies below, a crowded sprawl of striped awnings, stalls and carts, with the hum of bargaining drifting up on the wind. The smell of baking bread and frying onions rises with it. Out beyond the crenels the plains are quiet by comparison. The wall carries on north and south.
rooms.2913: The Trade Road lies below the outer wall here, a pale dusty ribbon between ditches, with a waymark stone at the verge and the ruts of wagons pressed deep in the dirt. Dust hangs over it in dry weather. The crenels frame a long view of the road running out across the plains toward the far hills. Walkers on the wall can go north or south from this spot.
rooms.2914: Carved stone spouts jut from the outer parapet at intervals, each shaped into a snarling hound with its mouth gaping to throw rain clear of the wall. Their muzzles are stained green and streaked white with lime. The coping between them is cracked and patched with lead. The wall continues north toward the corner and south along the parapet.
rooms.2915: A timber crane stands on the inner edge of the walk, a stout post and a swinging jib with a pulley and a coil of tarred rope, used to haul stores up from the street. Its arm is swung in and lashed to the post against the wind. The flags beneath are scuffed and stained with oil. The parapet leads north and also south from the crane.
rooms.2916: A little sentry box with a pitched shingle roof stands against the outer parapet, open on the side that faces the walk, with a narrow slot for a lantern cut in the back plank. Initials and crude drawings of ships cover the inside boards. The wind whistles through the gaps between the planks. Beyond the box the wall goes on north and south.
rooms.2917: A small stone garderobe juts from the outer face of the wall here, its low door hanging ajar on a leather hinge, and a sour smell clings about it despite the breeze. A drain channel runs down through the wall below. Nearby the coping is dark with damp. The battlements run north and south of this corner of the wall.
rooms.2918: Orange and grey lichen blooms across the parapet in rings, and tufts of stonecrop and thrift grow from the cracks in the coping. An iron lantern hangs from a post at the inner edge, its horn panes yellowed and cracked. The air up here is quiet and the wind comes in long even breaths. The walk lies open north and south.
rooms.2919: An alarm bell hangs in a timber frame beside the walk, a bronze bell as big as a barrel with a worn rope dangling from its clapper. Green stains streak its shoulder, and its note sounds faintly when the wind catches it. A cleared space around the frame keeps the way free. The wall-walk passes on north and south.
rooms.2920: A long scorched smear blackens the outer parapet where fire arrows once struck, the stone cracked and flaking beneath the soot. Fresh mortar fills a few of the worst gaps. Inward the crowded roofs fall away into a narrow lane of tiled gables. The walk runs north back along the battlements and south to a turn in the wall.
rooms.2921: A round turret caps the corner, its conical slate roof held up on stone pillars so that the wind sweeps freely through. A stone seat curves round the inside of the turret, and the mounting for a signal horn is bolted to a pillar. The long wall runs away on both sides, north back toward the gate and west along the next stretch. Beyond the crenels the plains stretch off to the hills in a haze.
rooms.2922: A windmill stands on a low rise out on the plains, its sails turning slowly with a creak that carries faintly even this high. Fields of barley and beans surround it in neat strips. The parapet underfoot is smooth and dry, and a crack in the coping holds a line of tufted grass. The walk runs east to the corner turret and west along the battlements.
rooms.2923: Over the inner parapet a slender bell tower topped with a green copper cap rises above the nearest roofs, and its notes come across the rooftops on the wind. The battlements here are cut by a row of deep crenels with stone seats built into the merlons. The walk leads east toward the corner and west toward the stair tower.
rooms.203072: A low stair tower caps the walk here, its roof of mossy green slate sloping over a door that opens on the top of the stair down to The Gate Of The Inner City. Orders for the wall are pinned on a weathered board by the doorpost, the ink faded to brown. A hooded cresset hangs from a bracket, black with old pitch. The wall-walk goes on east and west.
rooms.2924: A lone oak stands out on the plains beyond a hedgerow, its crown bent by the prevailing wind, with a low cairn of stones at its foot. The outer parapet is sound here and the crenels are wide enough to lean out. The flagstones are lightly dusted with chalky grit blown from the road. You can go east back to the stair tower, or west along the battlements.
rooms.2925: A machicolation juts out from the outer face, and the slots in the floor of the little projection show the base of the wall far below and the ditch at its foot. A cold draught rises through the slots. Stone corbels carry the projection, each carved with a blunt face. The walk goes east toward the stair tower and west to a turn in the wall.
rooms.2926: A tall flagstaff stands planted in the corner of the wall, its halyard drumming against the pole and the great banner of Garathorm streaming out stiff as a board in the wind. The parapet curves round the corner in a thick rounded bastion. The walk leads north along the next stretch of wall and east back along the battlements.
rooms.2927: The inner parapet is lower than the outer here, barely waist high, its coping rounded smooth by elbows. Below it the yards and back lanes of the city look small and tidy, with washing lines strung between chimneys. The outer face shows blank grey stone and tiny arrow slits. The wall-walk goes north along the battlements and south to the corner bastion.
rooms.2928: Moss and small ferns sprout from the joints of the coping, and long green stains show where rainwater runs down the outer face. A puddle fills a dip in the flagstones, rippling in the gusts. The air smells of damp stone and distant hay. The wall-walk stretches away to the north and the south.
rooms.2929: A black iron cauldron big enough to bathe a child hangs from a tripod beside the outer parapet, a bed of ash beneath it, for heating oil to pour on besiegers. Soot has darkened the crenel above it in a long streak. A trough of dry kindling stands against the wall. Past the tripod the battlements go on north and south.
rooms.2930: A timber hoarding has been built out over the outer face on stout corbels, a roofed gallery of planks with gaps in the floor and shutters on its front. The wood is silvered by weather and smells of pitch. Through the cracks you can see the foot of the wall far below. The walk heads north and south beneath the gallery.
rooms.2931: A bronze sundial is set into the inner parapet, its gnomon green with age and its numerals worn nearly smooth by many palms. When the sun is out its shadow slides across the dial in a thin dark line. The stone around it has been scrubbed pale. From the dial the walk runs north and also south.
rooms.2932: Rows of apple trees stand in an orchard beyond the ditch below the outer wall, their branches propped with forked poles. A low stone fence encloses them, and a path leads off through the grass toward the hills. The crenels here are fitted with worn stone sills. The battlements lead on to the north and to the south.
rooms.2933: A low stone hut squats against the inner parapet, its chimney leaking a thin thread of smoke and its shutters closed against the wind. A woodpile stacked beneath the eaves is capped with turf. The door is shut, and an iron boot-scraper stands beside it. The walk passes the hut going north or south.
rooms.2934: A weathered plaque is set into the inner parapet, its chiselled letters recording the raising of this stretch of the wall, the lines filled with moss and the last words worn away. A shallow gutter has been cut beneath it to carry the rain clear. The wall-walk runs on past the plaque, north and south alike.
rooms.2935: Smoke and the ring of hammers rise from a smithy's yard below the inner side, and the warm smell of charcoal and hot iron reaches the walk. Sparks from the forge chimney sometimes swirl up over the parapet. Out beyond the outer face the plains are green and still. Walkers may go north or south along the top of the wall.
rooms.2936: Here the wall stands at its tallest, where the ground outside dips into a hollow, and the outer face drops sheer to a dry ditch far below. The arrow slits are fitted with stout iron bars. The wind pulls hardest at your cloak in this stretch. The walk leads off both north and south.
rooms.2937: One merlon of the outer parapet has been split by lightning, the broken halves bound together with iron straps, and the stone around the crack is glassy and black. A fused patch in the flagging shows where the bolt struck. Rain gathers there and drains slowly through the crack. North and south the walk continues.
rooms.2938: In the inner wall an arched doorway has been bricked up, its outline picked out in paler mortar, so that it leads nowhere but into solid wall. Someone has chalked a tally of days on the infill. Beside it a stone water trough stands empty, cracked along its base. The battlements go on north and south from here.
rooms.2939: A pair of crenels are fitted with hinged wooden shutters painted with the city's sign, their leather hinges creaking whenever the wind pushes against them. Through the gaps you can see the plains stretching away to the dim line of the hills. The air smells of rain far off. You may follow the wall north or south.
rooms.2940: Ahead the roof of the tower over the gate rises above the walk, and the stone underfoot is stained dark with the ash of its brazier. A bracket of black iron holds a lantern at head height. The parapet on either side is thick and stout, built to guard the approach. The walk runs north to the tower and south along the wall.
rooms.203073: A broad watch platform ringed by a thick crenelled parapet stands over the gate, with a stair winding down from its flagged floor to the gate hall below. Above the stairhead a shadowed ledge under the tower's overhang makes a snug post for a sentry, with a stone stool and a view along the road. A brazier glows in an iron stand, and the wind snaps at a banner on the tower. The walk leads north and south from the platform.
rooms.2941: Beyond the outer parapet terraced rows of vines climb a gentle slope toward a small stone house, the leaves turning rust and gold along their trellises. The scent of crushed grapes sometimes rides up on the wind. The coping is smooth, with a groove where leaning arms have rested. North of the platform the walk goes on, and south it returns to the tower.
rooms.2942: A lead-lined channel runs along the inner foot of the parapet, carrying rainwater to a covered cistern whose stone lid has an iron ring. The lead is dented and patched with pewter. Over the roofs inward the grey sprawl of streets climbs to a cluster of tall slate-roofed spires. The wall runs north toward a corner and south toward the gate tower.
rooms.2943: Rust streaks the parapet below the iron cramps that hold the coping together, and the stone is stained a dull orange. Wind hums through an arrow loop that has lost its shutter. The inner side overlooks a long narrow court of drying racks and sheds. The walk goes north to the corner and south along the wall.
rooms.2944: A heavy drum of masonry forms the corner here, the walk curving around it and the parapet scratched with old sling-bullet scars. From the bend the wall can be seen running away in two long straight arms, one of them pale and narrowing into the haze. A stone spout drains the rain from the corner. The walk leads east along the battlements and south along the other arm.
rooms.2945: A row of iron hooks is set along the inner parapet for hanging festival banners, and they stand bare now, rusty and bent. Below the inner edge the steep roof of a great hall shows, its ridge capped with crow-stepped gables. The air is thin and cold at this height. The walk leads east toward the stair tower and west to the corner.
rooms.2946: Scratched into one of the flagstones is the grid of a game of nine men's morris, its lines worn pale by idle hours of play. The wind rushes up the outer face and over the coping in a steady sigh. Ahead you can make out the slate roof of a stairhead, with a thread of smoke curling from its brazier. The walk leads east to the stairhead and west along the battlements.
rooms.209005: The vintner's bedroom is small and low, its whitewashed walls leaning in under the slope of the roof and its dark beams close enough to touch. A narrow bed with a patched quilt of dyed wool stands under the shuttered window, and a pegged oak chest and a washstand fill the rest of the space. The air smells faintly of grape must and old wood smoke. A narrow stair leads down to the kitchen below.
rooms.209007: Brick vaults arch overhead in the vintner's cellar, and ranks of fat oak casks lie on cradles down both sides, their heads marked in chalk with the years of the vintages. The air is cool and still and sweet with the smell of old wine soaked into the stone. Steps climb up to the pressing house. A low door in the wall leads west to the storage room.
rooms.209008: Racks of dusty bottles climb the walls of this low storage room, their necks furred with grey, and everything is draped in cobwebs. Thick silken cables of web span from rack to rack and across the ceiling, as strong as ship's rope, and a dense white sheet of it clogs the far corner. Something large has spun here, and the dust is scuffed in wide ragged trails. The only way out is the door east to the cellar.

2908.description: The little carved woman holds a stone lamp in both hands, her face rubbed featureless by the touch of passing fingers. Someone has pushed a sprig of dried lavender into the crack beside her.

2909.keywords: mended breach newer stone mason mark
2909.description: The yellow stone is cleanly cut and closely jointed, far better work than the old wall around it. The mason's hammer-and-square mark is cut deep, as if the builder wished to be remembered for filling the gap.

2919.description: The bronze is thick and pitted, and a band of letters round its lip is too corroded to read. The frame is braced with iron straps, and its rope has been spliced many times.

2931.description: The dial is cast in bronze and bolted into the coping, its hour lines cut deep. The gnomon leans a little out of true, as though someone once used it as a handhold.

2934.description: The plaque says that this length of the wall was raised by the city's masons and its labouring people, and the date is cut in old numerals. The final line has crumbled into smooth stone.

209008.description: The strands are as thick as a thumb, grey and tacky with dust. Whatever spun them has dragged heavy things through the tangle, and torn threads hang in ragged loops.
